metadata.title: Game Development Engines — The Complete Open Guide

engines.name: Unity
engines.tagline: Cross-platform 2D and 3D engine widely used for indie, mobile, XR, and AA games.

dimensions.3d_note: Full-featured 3D PBR pipeline (URP, HDRP, Built-in)

engines.visual_scripting_note: Built-in Unity Visual Scripting (formerly Bolt)
engines.console_note: Console export (PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo Switch) requires Unity Pro/Enterprise and platform-holder approval.
engines.pricing_summary: Free Personal tier up to $200k trailing 12-month revenue/funding (splash screen optional in Unity 6); Pro $2,310/seat/year.

engines.name: Unreal Engine
engines.tagline: Source-available 3D engine with Blueprints visual scripting, C++ source access, and Lumen/Nanite rendering.

dimensions.3d_note: Lumen dynamic global illumination, Nanite virtualized geometry, and Niagara VFX

engines.visual_scripting_note: Blueprints node-based visual scripting is first-class and production-ready.
engines.console_note: Official console support requires registered developer status with Sony, Microsoft, or Nintendo.
engines.pricing_summary: Free to download and use; 5% royalty on gross revenue above $1,000,000 lifetime per game (waived on Epic Games Store).
engines.royalties: 5% above $1M lifetime gross revenue per product (0% on EGS sales)

engines.name: Godot
engines.tagline: Free, MIT-licensed open-source 2D and 3D engine with GDScript, C#, and C++ GDExtension.

dimensions.3d_note: Dedicated 2D pixel-coordinate renderer plus Forward+/Mobile/Compatibility 3D renderers

engines.visual_scripting_note: Built-in VisualScript was removed in Godot 4.0; third-party Orchestrator plugin adds visual scripting.
engines.console_note: No built-in console export due to MIT license vs NDA; consoles supported via third-party porting middleware (e.g., W4 Games).
engines.pricing_summary: 100% free and open-source forever under the MIT License with zero royalties.

engines.name: GameMaker
engines.tagline: 2D-focused commercial engine known for fast iteration, GML scripting, and GML Visual.

dimensions.3d_note: Primarily 2D; supports primitive 3D via vertex buffers and matrices, not a full 3D pipeline

engines.visual_scripting_note: GML Visual (node/block-based) is included free in all tiers and compiles to GML.
engines.console_note: Console exports require the Enterprise subscription ($79.99/mo or $799.99/yr) and platform-holder approval.
engines.pricing_summary: Free for non-commercial use; $99.99 one-time Professional license for commercial desktop/mobile/web; $79.99/mo Enterprise for consoles.
engines.royalties: 0% (one-time $99.99 Professional or Enterprise subscription for consoles)

engines.name: GDevelop
engines.tagline: Open-source no-code 2D/3D game engine powered by an intuitive event sheet system.

dimensions.3d_note: Includes native 3D objects, models, and behaviors; best suited for stylized/light 3D

engines.visual_scripting_note: Condition/Action event sheets allow full game creation without writing code.
engines.console_note: No native console export out of the box.
engines.pricing_summary: Core engine & manual exports are 100% free (MIT); optional cloud build/storage plans start around $4.99–$9.99/mo.
engines.royalties: 0% (MIT core; paid plans only for optional cloud builds/services)

engines.name: Phaser
engines.tagline: Fast, MIT-licensed 2D HTML5/WebGL framework for JavaScript and TypeScript developers.

dimensions.3d_note: Strictly 2D (WebGL & Canvas)

engines.visual_scripting_note: Code-first framework; optional paid Phaser Editor adds visual scene layout.
engines.console_note: Desktop/mobile via Electron/Capacitor wrappers; not designed for native console releases.
engines.pricing_summary: 100% free and open-source (MIT); optional Phaser Editor commercial tooling has paid plans.

engines.name: Construct 3
engines.tagline: Browser-based 2D game engine using event sheets with optional JavaScript/TypeScript.

dimensions.3d_note: 2D-first with basic 3D camera/shape/mesh distortion features

engines.visual_scripting_note: Visual event sheets are the primary workflow.
engines.console_note: Xbox export supported via UWP/WebView2; other consoles via third-party wrappers.
engines.pricing_summary: Free edition limited to 25 events (no commercial export); Personal subscription ~$15.99/mo or ~$119/yr.

engines.name: Defold
engines.tagline: Lightweight, source-available Lua-based 2D/3D engine backed by the Defold Foundation.

dimensions.3d_note: Strong 2D focus with native 3D mesh, PBR, and physics support

engines.visual_scripting_note: Code-driven using Lua.
engines.console_note: Official Nintendo Switch, PS4, PS5, and Xbox support for approved console developers.
engines.pricing_summary: 100% free forever with zero royalties, guaranteed by the Defold Foundation charter.

engines.name: RPG Maker MZ
engines.tagline: Specialized 2D tilemap engine designed for classic JRPGs with zero coding required.

dimensions.3d_note: Strictly 2D tile-based RPG engine

engines.visual_scripting_note: Built-in database, map editor, and event command system.
engines.console_note: Mobile requires Cordova/Capacitor wrapping; consoles require third-party porting.
engines.pricing_summary: $69.99–$79.99 one-time purchase (frequently discounted); zero royalties.

engines.name: Ren'Py
engines.tagline: Free, MIT-licensed visual novel engine powered by Python and a simple dialogue script.

dimensions.3d_note: 2D narrative/UI engine with 3D camera transforms for parallax

engines.visual_scripting_note: Uses human-readable dialogue script syntax, very accessible to non-programmers.
engines.console_note: Consoles require third-party porting (e.g., Ratalaika or Serenity Forge).
engines.pricing_summary: 100% free and open-source with zero royalties.

engines.name: LÖVE (Love2D)
engines.tagline: Minimalist, zlib-licensed 2D game framework using Lua.

dimensions.3d_note: 2D framework; custom 3D possible via shaders/meshes

engines.visual_scripting_note: Code-only framework (no built-in GUI editor).
engines.console_note: No official console export; community ports exist for homebrew/consoles via partners.
engines.pricing_summary: 100% free and open-source (zlib license) with zero royalties.

engines.name: Bevy
engines.tagline: Data-driven Entity Component System (ECS) game engine built in Rust under MIT/Apache 2.0.

dimensions.3d_note: PBR 3D rendering, global illumination experiments, and 2D sprite/tilemap support

engines.visual_scripting_note: Code-first ECS architecture; visual editor is under active community/official development.
engines.console_note: No official console targets yet due to NDA/Rust toolchain constraints.
engines.pricing_summary: 100% free and open-source forever (MIT / Apache 2.0).

engines.name: Cocos Creator
engines.tagline: Open-core 2D/3D engine with TypeScript scripting, popular for mobile and HTML5 mini-games.

dimensions.3d_note: Supports full 3D PBR rendering alongside industry-proven 2D tools

engines.visual_scripting_note: Component-based editor with TypeScript scripting.
engines.console_note: Primarily targets mobile, desktop, and web/mini-game platforms.
engines.pricing_summary: 100% free with zero royalties; optional enterprise VIP support and marketplace assets.

engines.name: MonoGame
engines.tagline: Open-source C# framework (successor to Microsoft XNA) for 2D and 3D cross-platform games.

dimensions.3d_note: Code-level 2D SpriteBatch and 3D GraphicsDevice APIs

engines.visual_scripting_note: Code-only framework (bring your own level editor like Tiled or LDtk).
engines.console_note: Proven console track record (Switch, PlayStation, Xbox) for registered console developers.
engines.pricing_summary: 100% free and open-source (Ms-PL) with zero royalties.

engines.name: Three.js
engines.tagline: The most widely used open-source WebGL/WebGPU 3D library for browser games and experiences.

dimensions.3d_note: Full WebGL 2 & WebGPU 3D rendering library

engines.visual_scripting_note: Code-first library with an optional online scene editor.
engines.console_note: Browser-first; native apps via Electron/Capacitor.
engines.pricing_summary: 100% free and open-source (MIT).

engines.name: Babylon.js
engines.tagline: Complete, MIT-licensed WebGL/WebGPU 3D engine with physics, XR, and node material editor.

dimensions.3d_note: Full 3D PBR, WebGPU, Havok physics integration, and WebXR

engines.visual_scripting_note: Includes visual Node Material Editor & GUI Editor; gameplay is coded in TS/JS.
engines.console_note: Browser-first; native via Babylon Native / Electron.
engines.pricing_summary: 100% free and open-source (Apache 2.0).

engines.name: PlayCanvas
engines.tagline: Cloud-hosted collaborative 3D HTML5/WebGL engine with an MIT open-source runtime.

dimensions.3d_note: Optimized 3D WebGL/WebGPU engine built for instant-load browser games

engines.visual_scripting_note: Visual scene/hierarchy editor with JS/TS scripting.
engines.console_note: Focused on WebGL, mobile instant games, and playable ads.
engines.pricing_summary: Free tier for public projects; Personal ($15/mo) and Organization ($50/seat/mo) for private cloud projects.

engines.name: PixiJS
engines.tagline: MIT-licensed 2D WebGL and WebGPU rendering library for web games and interactive apps.

dimensions.3d_note: Pure 2D hardware-accelerated renderer

engines.visual_scripting_note: Rendering library only; no built-in editor.
engines.console_note: Web-first; wrap with Electron/Capacitor for desktop/mobile.
engines.pricing_summary: 100% free and open-source (MIT).

engines.name: CRYENGINE
engines.tagline: High-end 3D engine known for realistic outdoor environments and real-time lighting.

dimensions.3d_note: AAA 3D rendering with SVOGI global illumination

engines.visual_scripting_note: Schematyc visual scripting system.
engines.console_note: Console support for registered developers.
engines.pricing_summary: Free to start; 5% royalty above $5,000 annual revenue per project.

engines.name: O3DE (Open 3D Engine)
engines.tagline: Linux Foundation Apache 2.0 / MIT open-source AAA-grade 3D engine evolved from Lumberyard.

dimensions.3d_note: Atom photorealistic PBR renderer, modular Gem architecture

engines.visual_scripting_note: Script Canvas node-based visual scripting.
engines.console_note: No out-of-the-box public console exports.
engines.pricing_summary: 100% free and open-source (Apache 2.0 / MIT) with zero royalties.

engines.name: Stride
engines.tagline: MIT-licensed open-source C# 2D/3D engine with a visual editor similar to Unity.

dimensions.3d_note: Modern C#/.NET 3D PBR pipeline with Vulkan/Direct3D 12

engines.visual_scripting_note: Code-first C#/.NET 8+ scripting inside Game Studio.
engines.console_note: No official public console export.
engines.pricing_summary: 100% free and open-source (MIT) with zero royalties.

engines.name: Solar2D
engines.tagline: MIT-licensed open-source Lua 2D engine (formerly Corona SDK) built for fast mobile games.

dimensions.3d_note: Strictly 2D

engines.visual_scripting_note: Code-first Lua workflow with instant live simulator.
engines.console_note: Targets mobile, desktop, and HTML5; no console support.
engines.pricing_summary: 100% free and open-source (MIT) with zero royalties.

engines.name: libGDX
engines.tagline: Mature, Apache 2.0-licensed Java/Kotlin cross-platform game development framework.

dimensions.3d_note: Strong 2D APIs plus 3D rendering support

engines.visual_scripting_note: Code-only framework.
engines.console_note: Console ports possible via third-party tools like SwitchGDX / RoboVM.
engines.pricing_summary: 100% free and open-source (Apache 2.0) with zero royalties.

engines.name: HaxeFlixel
engines.tagline: MIT-licensed 2D Haxe game engine popular for retro pixel-art and Newgrounds-style games.

dimensions.3d_note: Strictly 2D

engines.visual_scripting_note: Code-first framework.
engines.console_note: Consoles possible via Haxe/C++ Lime targets with NDA.
engines.pricing_summary: 100% free and open-source (MIT) with zero royalties.

engines.name: PICO-8
engines.tagline: Fantasy console for making, sharing, and playing tiny retro 2D pixel-art games in Lua.

dimensions.3d_note: 128x128 16-color 2D fantasy console

engines.visual_scripting_note: Includes built-in sprite, map, SFX, and music editors alongside Lua code.
engines.console_note: Exports standalone HTML5/desktop binaries; playable in web browsers via cartridges.
engines.pricing_summary: $14.99 one-time purchase (Free Education web edition available); zero royalties.
